title: Triangle
statement_short: Given a triangle array, return the minimum path sum from top to bottom. For each step, you may move to adjacent numbers on the row below.
hint: Triangle length up to 200 permits bottom-up grid state transitions to compute min path sum.
keywords: adjacent numbers on the row below
why_not: Right: 2D DP computes minimum path sums bottom-up by taking min(dp[row+1][col], dp[row+1][col+1]) + triangle[row][col] in O(n^2) time and O(n) space. Not Graph BFS: Level-order grid queue search works, but 2D DP handles overlapping subproblem states directly. Not Greedy: Picking the smaller adjacent element locally fails when a larger node leads to smaller overall path sums later. Not Backtracking: Exploring all paths recursively takes exponential O(2^n) time.
